nodes.title: Autoscaling
nodes.summary: Automatically adding compute capacity when the workload grows and removing it when the workload shrinks.

nodes.title: Availability Zone
nodes.summary: One of several physically separate data centers within a cloud region, each with independent power and networking.

nodes.title: Backfill
nodes.summary: Running a pipeline over past time periods to fill in or recompute historical data.

nodes.title: Broadcast Join
nodes.summary: A join strategy that copies a small table to every executor so the large table does not have to be shuffled.

nodes.title: CI-CD

nodes.title: Caching
nodes.summary: Storing a copy of data or query results in faster storage so repeated requests return sooner.

nodes.title: Checkpoint
nodes.summary: A saved record of a job's progress and state, used to resume after a failure without reprocessing or losing data.

nodes.title: Cluster
nodes.summary: A group of computers that work together as one system; Databricks now mostly calls these compute resources.

nodes.title: Compression
nodes.summary: Encoding data in fewer bytes to reduce storage and read time, at the cost of CPU work to compress and decompress.

nodes.title: Container
nodes.summary: A packaged application with its dependencies that runs the same way on any host; in Azure Storage, also the top-level folder of a storage account.

nodes.title: Cutover
nodes.summary: The planned point in a migration when users and workloads switch from the old system to the new one.
links_out: Running Old and New in Parallel

nodes.title: DAG
nodes.summary: A directed acyclic graph: a set of steps connected by one-way dependencies with no loops, used to order pipeline and query work.

nodes.title: Dashboard
nodes.summary: A single view of charts, tables, and key metrics that summarizes the state of a business or system.
links_out: Connecting Tableau and Other BI Tools

nodes.title: Data Catalog
nodes.summary: A searchable inventory of an organization's datasets with their descriptions, owners, lineage, and access rules.

nodes.title: Data Governance
nodes.summary: The policies and controls that determine who can use which data, how it is protected, and whether it can be trusted.

nodes.title: Data Lake vs Data Swamp
nodes.summary: A data lake stores raw data of any type in cheap storage; a data swamp is a data lake that has become unusable for lack of organization and governance.

nodes.title: Data Mart
nodes.summary: A subset of a data warehouse modeled for one business area, such as sales or finance.

nodes.title: Data Mesh
nodes.summary: A decentralized approach in which business domains own their data and publish it as products under shared governance.

nodes.title: Data Pipeline
nodes.summary: An automated sequence of steps that moves data from its sources to where it is used, transforming it along the way.

nodes.title: Data Quality
nodes.summary: The degree to which data is accurate, complete, timely, and consistent enough for its intended use.

nodes.title: Data Skew
nodes.summary: An uneven distribution of data across partitions that leaves a few tasks with most of the work.

nodes.title: Data Skipping
nodes.summary: Avoiding reads of files that cannot contain matching rows, using per-file column statistics such as minimum and maximum values.

nodes.title: Data Type
nodes.summary: The kind of value a column can hold, such as integers, decimals, strings, dates, or nested structures.

nodes.title: Denormalization
nodes.summary: Storing redundant copies of data in wider tables so queries need fewer joins.

nodes.title: Dimension Table
nodes.summary: A table of descriptive attributes, such as customer, product, or date, that fact tables reference by key.

nodes.title: Drift
nodes.summary: A change over time in data or in the relationship a model learned, which degrades results without any code change.

nodes.title: Egress
nodes.summary: Network traffic leaving a network, region, or cloud; it can incur transfer charges and is a common security control point.

nodes.title: Embedding
nodes.summary: A vector of numbers that represents the meaning of text, images, or other items, so similar items have nearby vectors.

nodes.title: Encryption at Rest
nodes.summary: Encrypting stored data so it cannot be read without the key, even with direct access to the storage.

nodes.title: Encryption in Transit
nodes.summary: Encrypting data while it moves across a network, usually with TLS, so intermediaries cannot read or alter it.

nodes.title: Event
nodes.summary: A timestamped record that something happened, such as a click, payment, or sensor reading.

nodes.title: Exactly-Once Processing
nodes.summary: A guarantee that each input affects the final result exactly once, with no loss and no duplication, even after failures.

nodes.title: Fact Table
nodes.summary: The central table in a star schema that records business events and their numeric measures.

nodes.title: Fault Tolerance
nodes.summary: The ability of a system to continue operating, or recover without data loss, when a component fails.

nodes.title: Feature
nodes.summary: A measurable input variable that a machine-learning model uses to make predictions.

nodes.title: Firewall
nodes.summary: A network control that allows or blocks traffic according to rules on source, destination, port, and protocol.

nodes.title: GDPR
nodes.summary: The European Union regulation that governs how personal data of people in the EU and EEA is collected, processed, and erased.

nodes.title: GPU
nodes.summary: A graphics processing unit: a processor with thousands of parallel cores, used to train and run deep-learning models and LLMs.

nodes.title: Git
nodes.summary: A distributed version-control system that records every change to code and supports parallel work through branches.

nodes.title: HIPAA
nodes.summary: The US healthcare law that sets national standards for protecting the privacy and security of protected health information (PHI).
aliases: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act

nodes.title: Hallucination
nodes.summary: Output from an AI model that is false or unsupported but presented as fact.

nodes.title: IAM
nodes.summary: Identity and access management: the systems and policies that establish who a user or service is and what it is allowed to do.

nodes.title: Idempotency
nodes.summary: The property of an operation that produces the same result whether it runs once or many times, which makes retries safe.

nodes.title: Identity Provider
nodes.summary: The service that stores an organization's user accounts and groups and authenticates sign-ins for other applications.

nodes.title: Index
nodes.summary: A data structure that lets a database locate rows without scanning the whole table.

nodes.title: Inference
nodes.summary: Using a trained model to produce predictions or generated output for new inputs.

nodes.title: Infrastructure as Code
nodes.summary: Defining infrastructure such as workspaces, networks, and permissions in version-controlled files that a tool applies automatically.

nodes.title: Ingestion
nodes.summary: Copying data from source systems, such as applications, databases, files, and streams, into the data platform.

nodes.title: IoT
nodes.summary: The Internet of Things: physical devices such as sensors, meters, and machines that send data over a network.

nodes.title: JDBC and ODBC
nodes.summary: Standard database connectivity interfaces that let BI tools, spreadsheets, and applications run SQL against a database through a driver.
links_out: Connecting Tableau and Other BI Tools

nodes.title: JVM
nodes.summary: The Java Virtual Machine: the runtime that executes Java and Scala bytecode, and the process in which Spark's driver and executors run.

nodes.title: Join
nodes.summary: A query operation that combines rows from two tables based on matching values in one or more columns.

nodes.title: KPI
nodes.summary: A key performance indicator: one number a business watches to know whether it is on track.

nodes.title: Kubernetes
nodes.summary: Open-source software that runs and restarts containers across a fleet of machines.

nodes.title: LLM
nodes.summary: A large language model: an AI trained on huge amounts of text that predicts and generates language.

nodes.title: Label
nodes.summary: The right answer attached to a training example, which a machine learning model learns to predict.

nodes.title: Latency
nodes.summary: The waiting time between asking for something and getting the answer.

nodes.title: Least Privilege
nodes.summary: Give each person or program only the access it needs for its job, and nothing more.

nodes.title: Lift and Shift
nodes.summary: Moving a system to a new platform as-is, without redesigning it.
links_out: Running Old and New in Parallel

nodes.title: Linux Foundation
nodes.summary: A nonprofit that hosts and governs major open-source projects, including Delta Lake, MLflow, and Unity Catalog OSS.

nodes.title: Managed Identity
nodes.summary: An Azure identity that Azure creates and rotates for a resource, so no passwords or keys are stored.

nodes.title: Message Queue
nodes.summary: A holding line for messages, so one system can send data and another can pick it up later.

nodes.title: Metadata
nodes.summary: Data about data: names, types, owners, sizes, locations, and history of your tables and files.

nodes.title: Model
nodes.summary: A trained program that turns inputs into a prediction or generated output.

nodes.title: Node
nodes.summary: One computer in a group of computers that work together.

nodes.title: Normalization
nodes.summary: Splitting data into separate related tables so each fact is stored only once.

nodes.title: Null
nodes.summary: The empty value: Python's None and SQL's NULL mean the value is missing or unknown.

nodes.title: OAuth
nodes.summary: An open standard for handing out short-lived access tokens instead of sharing passwords.

nodes.title: Open Source
nodes.summary: Software whose source code anyone can read, use, change, and share under a public license.
links_out: Open Source vs Databricks - Who Replaced What

nodes.title: Orchestration
nodes.summary: Running the steps of a data process in the right order, on schedule, with retries and alerts.

nodes.title: Overfitting
nodes.summary: When a model memorizes its training data and then does badly on new data.

nodes.title: PII
nodes.summary: Personally identifiable information: any data that can identify a specific person.

nodes.title: Pandas
nodes.summary: The most popular Python library for working with tables of data on one computer.

nodes.title: Partition Pruning
nodes.summary: Skipping whole folders of a table because the query's filter shows they cannot contain matching rows.

nodes.title: Prompt
nodes.summary: The text instructions and context you give a language model to get an answer.

nodes.title: Proof of Concept
nodes.summary: A small, time-boxed trial that tests whether a tool or idea works before committing to it.

nodes.title: Public vs Private IP
nodes.summary: A public IP address is reachable from the internet; a private one works only inside a private network.

nodes.title: Query
nodes.summary: A request to read or change data, usually written in SQL.

nodes.title: REST
nodes.summary: A common style of web API where programs request and change resources over HTTP with GET, POST, and similar verbs.

nodes.title: Region
nodes.summary: A geographic area where a cloud provider runs its data centers, such as East US or Frankfurt.

nodes.title: Replication
nodes.summary: Keeping copies of data in more than one place so it survives failures or is closer to users.

nodes.title: Reverse ETL
nodes.summary: Copying cleaned data from the analytics platform back into the business tools people use every day.

nodes.title: Role-Based Access Control
nodes.summary: Granting permissions to roles or groups, then putting people in those groups, instead of granting to each person.

nodes.title: SLA
nodes.summary: A service level agreement: a written promise about uptime, speed, or delivery time, often with penalties if missed.

nodes.title: SOC 2
nodes.summary: An independent audit report showing a service provider protects customer data with proper security controls.

nodes.title: SaaS PaaS and IaaS
nodes.summary: Three levels of cloud service: rent raw machines (IaaS), a platform to build on (PaaS), or finished software (SaaS).

nodes.title: Scala
nodes.summary: A programming language for the Java virtual machine, and the language Apache Spark itself is written in.
links_out: AMPLab and the Birth of Spark

nodes.title: Scalability
nodes.summary: How well a system keeps working as data, users, or traffic grow.

nodes.title: Schema
nodes.summary: The structure of data (column names and types), and in Databricks also a folder-like container of tables.

nodes.title: Semantic Layer
nodes.summary: A shared layer of business definitions (revenue, active customer) that every tool reads from, so numbers match.

nodes.title: Serialization
nodes.summary: Turning data or objects in memory into bytes so they can be stored or sent, and back again.

nodes.title: Single Source of Truth
nodes.summary: One agreed, trusted place for each piece of data, so everyone works from the same numbers.

nodes.title: Spill
nodes.summary: When Spark runs out of memory for a task and writes temporary data to disk, which slows the job.

nodes.title: Spot Instances
nodes.summary: Spare cloud machines sold at a discount that the cloud can take back at short notice.

nodes.title: Subnet
nodes.summary: A smaller slice of a private cloud network, with its own range of IP addresses.

nodes.title: Throughput
nodes.summary: How much work a system finishes per unit of time, such as rows per second or queries per minute.

nodes.title: Token
nodes.summary: Two meanings: a digital pass that proves who you are, or a small chunk of text that a language model reads and writes.

nodes.title: Total Cost of Ownership
nodes.summary: The full cost of a system over its life: licenses and cloud bills plus people, maintenance, and migration.
links_out: Databricks vs Alternatives for Small Teams
Estimating Costs for a Small Business

nodes.title: Training
nodes.summary: The process of a machine learning model learning patterns from example data.

nodes.title: UDF
nodes.summary: A user-defined function: your own code that runs inside a query like a built-in function.

nodes.title: VPC and VNet
nodes.summary: Your own private, isolated network inside a cloud: called a VPC on AWS and Google Cloud, and a VNet on Azure.

nodes.title: Vendor Lock-In
nodes.summary: Being so tied to one vendor's product that leaving would be slow, costly, or risky.
links_out: Databricks vs Alternatives for Small Teams

nodes.title: Virtual Machine
nodes.summary: A software computer that runs on a shared physical server, rented by the hour from a cloud provider.

nodes.title: Watermark
nodes.summary: In streaming, a moving cutoff that says how late an event may arrive and still be counted.

nodes.title: Webhook
nodes.summary: An automatic web message one system sends to another when something happens.

nodes.title: YAML
nodes.summary: A plain-text format for configuration files that uses indentation instead of brackets.

nodes.title: Z-Ordering
nodes.summary: A Delta Lake technique that sorts related values into the same files so queries can skip more files.

nodes.title: Zero-Copy
nodes.summary: Using or sharing data where it already sits, without making a physical duplicate.
